title: Investigating the associations between neurodevelopmental and psychiatric genetic liability and adverse social and functional outcomes across childhood, adolescence and young-adulthood
title_zh: 探究神经发育与精神疾病遗传易感性与儿童、青少年及青年期社会与功能结果的关联
abstract: Abstract Neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions often originate in youth and can lead to adverse social and functional outcomes. It is unclear whether these associations are driven by genetic liability to these conditions, with possible developmental differences. We examined multivariable associations between polygenic scores (PGS) for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, anxiety and three outcomes: peer problems, educational attainment/employment and suicidality, in childhood, adolescence and young-adulthood. Data were analysed from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children; outcomes at ages 10–13, 16 and 24–25 years. ADHD PGS was associated with peer problems (OR = 1.13, p = 0.020; OR = 1.21, p < 0.0001; OR = 1.14, p = 0.010) and lower educational attainment/employment in childhood, adolescence and young-adulthood(OR = 1.40, p < 0.0001; OR = 1.62, p < 0.0001; OR = 1.29, p = 0.005 respectively) and suicidality in childhood (OR = 1.13, p = 0.030). ASD PGS was associated with peer problems and suicidality in childhood (OR = 1.24, p < 0.0001; OR = 1.24, p = <0.0001) and greater educational attainment in childhood and adolescence (OR = 0.88, p = 0.004; OR = 0.77, p = 0.007). Depression PGS was associated with peer problems in childhood and young-adulthood (OR = 1.18, p = 0.003; OR = 1.21, p < 0.0001), and poorer educational attainment/employment and suicidality in adolescence (OR = 1.39, p = 0.004; OR = 1.28, p < 0.0001) and young-adulthood (OR = 1.26, p = 0.017; OR = 1.42, p < 0.0001). We did not find strong evidence of associations for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or anxiety PGS. These findings suggest that genetic liability to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions are associated with a range of social/functional outcomes, although the strength and direction of association vary by PGS, outcome and development stage. This highlights the importance of examining genetic liability to multiple conditions simultaneously and of a developmental perspective.
abstract_zh: 摘要：神经发育和精神疾病常在青少年时期出现，可能导致不良的社会和功能结果。尚不清楚这些关联是否由对这些疾病的遗传易感性驱动，并可能存在发育差异。我们检验了多变量关联，使用注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）、自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）、精神分裂症、双相情感障碍、抑郁症、焦虑症的多基因风险评分（PGS）与三种结果：同伴问题、教育成就/就业和自杀倾向，在儿童、青少年和青年期的关联。数据来自Avon纵向研究（Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children），结果测量时间为10–13岁、16岁和24–25岁。ADHD PGS 与同伴问题相关（OR = 1.13, p = 0.020；OR = 1.21, p < 0.0001；OR = 1.14, p = 0.010），并在儿童、青少年和青年期与较低的教育成就/就业相关（OR = 1.40, p < 0.0001；OR = 1.62, p < 0.0001；OR = 1.29, p = 0.005），以及儿童期的自杀倾向（OR = 1.13, p = 0.030）。ASD PGS 与儿童期的同伴问题和自杀倾向相关（OR = 1.24, p < 0.0001；OR = 1.24, p < 0.0001），并与儿童和青少年期更高的教育成就相关（OR = 0.88, p = 0.004；OR = 0.77, p = 0.007）。抑郁症 PGS 与儿童和青年期的同伴问题相关（OR = 1.18, p = 0.003；OR = 1.21, p < 0.0001），以及青少年期和青年期的教育成就/就业下降和自杀倾向（青少年期：OR = 1.39, p = 0.004；OR = 1.28, p < 0.0001；青年期：OR = 1.26, p = 0.017；OR = 1.42, p < 0.0001）。我们未发现精神分裂症、双相情感障碍或焦虑症 PGS 与结果之间的强关联。结果表明，神经发育和精神疾病的遗传易感性与多种社会/功能结果相关，但关联的强度和方向因 PGS、结果和发展阶段而异。这强调了同时考察多种疾病遗传易感性以及发展视角的重要性。
